summary: DNS64-synthesized NXDOMAIN from branch SD‑WAN causing token refresh loop and intermittent gRPC stalls on private deployment
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent authentication failures and repeated token refresh attempts originating from a branch SD‑WAN site. Symptom onset correlates with heavy outbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic windows. Impact: Several customer services that call Redwood API intermittently get 401 from control plane and exhibit gRPC stalls in serving nodes; application-level retries amplify traffic and increase latency for downstream requests. Environment: FinEdge private deployment via VPCE across us-west-2; affected nodes in private subnet (subnet-abc123) for branch office IP block 198.51.100.0/24. Primary resolver is an on‑prem DNS64 gateway (branch SD‑WAN vendor provided).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From branch office behind SD‑WAN, initiate a token refresh against control plane using customer app (observed by customer).
2) Simulate high outbound HTTP traffic to CDN to reproduce timing (customer reports failure windows align with nightly batch),
3) Observe repeated 401 errors in control plane logs followed by bursty gRPC pauses on serving nodes (10-30s windows).
4) Collect DNS resolution from branch resolver for control-plane hostnames; DNS64 synthesizes AAAA responses for names that have A-only behavior and returns NXDOMAIN for some internal VPCE hostnames.
logs: 2026-03-10T03:12:11Z control-plane-auth ERROR token refresh failed 401 client_id=fedge-app-2 trace=abc123
2026-03-10T03:12:20Z serving-node-17 WARN grpc stream stalled kv-cache-miss host=svc-redwood-private.vpce.local
dnsdump: query svc-redwood-private.vpce.local IN AAAA -> response NXDOMAIN (synthesized by dns64 gateway)
tcpdump: retransmit from client 198.51.100.45 -> control-plane 443: TLS handshake restarted after 2 retransmits
investigation_notes: 03-10 04:00 PST: Eng (Miguel) onboarded packet captures from customer; observed DNS64 gateway rewriting and NXDOMAIN responses for split-horizon names.
03-10 07:32 PST: CS confirmed issue only from branch SD‑WAN; other sites (direct WAN) unaffected.

Hypothesis: DNS64 gateway is synthesizing AAAA or returning NXDOMAIN for internal VPCE names which confuses client library DNS logic, causing it to treat control-plane endpoint as unreachable and retry auth token flow repeatedly.
Observed correlation between heavy outbound bursts and SD‑WAN path changes causing DNS cache churn and transient NXDOMAIN hits.
Grafana dashboards: control-plane auth 401 spike at 2026-03-10T03:11-03:20Z; serving node grpc stalled increased p95 latency from 120ms->2.3s.
Packet captures and dns logs uploaded to S3: s3://support-artifacts/finedge/SUP-421358/pcap-20260310.zip
Checked RBAC/token TTL: no regression in token signing; failure appears upstream of auth acceptance (client never completed TLS session for some attempts).
Reproduced locally by forcing IPv6 lookup path using dns64-resolver: client falls back incorrectly and stalls at gRPC due to ALPN/TLS expectations mismatch on presigned URL fetch paths.
comments: 2026-03-10 05:00 UTC - Leah Chen (Support): Logged initial report after customer escalated to CS. Collected DNS samples and packet captures. Asked customer to confirm if resolver is DNS64/DNS64+NAT64; customer confirmed DNS64 from SD‑WAN appliance.

2026-03-10 08:15 UTC - Miguel Santos (SRE): Packet capture shows DNS64 synthesizing AAAA for A-only control-plane endpoints and NXDOMAIN for some split-horizon records. Hypothesis: client attempts IPv6 path, fails TLS ALPN expectations on presigned S3 fetch, then triggers an auth retry loop.

2026-03-11 10:22 UTC - FinEdge NetOps (customer): Temporarily disabled DNS64 on branch resolver; observed immediate drop in 401 spikes and gRPC stalls resolved during test window. Requesting guidance on long-term fix and Redwood mitigation.

2026-03-12 14:40 UTC - Miguel Santos (SRE): Implemented temporary control-plane tolerant logic in staging that ignores NXDOMAIN from known dns64 resolvers for VPCE internal hostnames. Will prepare PR to add resolver signature detection and fallback to A-only resolution path.
2026-03-12 15:05 UTC - Leah Chen (Support): Notified customer of workaround steps and asked for maintenance window to test Redwood fix in their staging environment.
resolution: Workaround: Customer disabled DNS64 at branch resolver which reduced failures immediately. Temporary Redwood mitigation: add resolver-detection guardrail in control-plane client libraries to prefer A-only path for VPCE internal hostnames and avoid treating DNS64-synthesized NXDOMAIN as terminal for auth flows. Planned long-term fix: patch client DNS fallback logic and release SDK patch (PR linked) and update support runbook with DNS64 detection and customer guidance. Follow-up: schedule rolling release of control-plane client library change (canary -> prod) and coordinate maintenance window with FinEdge NetOps.
next_steps: 1) Merge PR and run canary in staging control-plane (owner: Miguel Santos).
2) Customer to re-enable DNS64 in a controlled test after patch to verify stable behavior (owner: FinEdge NetOps).
3) Publish support KB article with detection heuristics and recommended resolver config for private deployments.
